newsitem.title: USA: U.S. midweek cash lumber review - April 2.
newsitem.headline: U.S. midweek cash lumber review - April 2.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:

Comment - Carryover from a more active pace late last week gave many lumber prices an upward slant through Tuesday, Random Lengths said in its midweek market update. Prices of most dry species strengthened as the feared Canadian "wall of wood" anticipated by many dealers from April 1 failed to develop.

The Northeast was expected to recover quickly from Monday's snowstorm, while fair weather prevailed in most other regions. OSB prices remained soft. Southern Pine plywood production returned to normal as the log crunch in the region eased.

Western S-P-F prices maintained an upward tilt. Buying was off from last week's pace but just about matched producers' offerings, Random Lengths said. Mill shipping times were usually out a couple of weeks, refuting the "wall of wood" theory tied to the start of the new Canada quota shipments year on April 1.
Some Western buyers said #2&Btr 2x8 was tough to find. Stud prices trended higher but were scattered over a $20 range.

Eastern S-P-F markets were active in trading carried over from last week's late rally. Mills raised prices $10 or more of #1&2 items, but advances varied among individual producers. Wholesalers took longer positions when they could book at the low end of price spreads. Large block orders were noticeably absent except for a few deals on studs, Random Lengths said.

Southern Pine sales were steady in early trading. Most mills started with comfortable order files and sold enough to maintain them. Prices held or edged higher, with 2x4 lagging the other widths. The 2x6 sold well, especially in the central zone.
Inland dimension prices rose as demand buoyed order files.
Inland mills said they could ship odds and ends quickly but decent tallies for shipments before mid-April were tight. Studs edged up. Ponderosa Pine #2&Btr and #4 1x12 prices softened.

Coast Hem-Fir and dry Douglas fir sales were steady to better, lifting many prices. The wides were the best sellers, with #2&Btr 2x10 the standout. Lack of availability contributed to the higher prices in fir as several mills chose not to dry their stock. Stud prices rose $5 in both species.

Most Southern Pine plywood mills held quotes on sheathing and underlayments but were susceptible to $3-5 counters. Demand was spotty with sales to the Northeast especially slow due to the weather. High-grade panel prices strengthened.

Fir plywood CDX prices remained soft overall but pending curtailments and a slightly better sales pace perked up demand. Boise Cascade announced it would shut down its Yakima mill for 2-4 weeks because of temporary log supply problems. One immediate result was a pick up in sales of 1/2-inch 3-ply.

OSB sales continued to sputter and prices were either flat or lower. Most purchases were on a hand-to-mouth basis. Block inquiries circulated but mills were not inclined to book volumes at current levels. Traders listened for curtailments but heard of none, Random Lengths said.
